indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.5.4.1: Know that climate change is one of the most important environmental issues facing the world today and is a long-term change in the pattern of average weather of a specific region of the earth
indicator.objective: Identify human activities that pollute the atmosphere

skills.description: Identify human activities that pollute the atmosphere
Describe how these activities pollute the air
Explain how air pollution affects life
Suggest ways to reduce air pollution

misconceptions: Burning rubbish is safe because it disappears.
Air pollution only happens in cities.
Cutting down trees helps the atmosphere.
Climate change is not related to human activities.

questions.stem: Which of these human activities pollutes the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Burning rubbish releases smoke and harmful gases into the air, polluting the atmosphere.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think burning is safe.

questions.stem: Which of these releases harmful gases into the air?
questions.explanation: Car exhaust fumes release harmful gases like carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide, polluting the atmosphere.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider cars as polluters.

questions.stem: What happens to the air when people burn bushes?
questions.explanation: Bush burning releases smoke and harmful particles into the air, causing air pollution.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think burning cleans the air.

questions.stem: How does air pollution affect people's health?
hints: Dirty air goes into the lungs.
questions.explanation: Air pollution can cause coughing, asthma, and other breathing problems.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not link air pollution to health.

questions.stem: Which of these helps reduce air pollution?
questions.explanation: Planting trees helps clean the air by absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know trees improve air quality.

questions.stem: How does smoke from factories pollute the atmosphere?
options: It releases harmful gases and particles into the air
It removes oxygen from the air
It turns the air into water
questions.explanation: Factory smoke releases pollutants like carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, and particulate matter into the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think factory smoke is harmless.

questions.stem: Why is it harmful to burn rubbish in the open air?
options: It releases toxic smoke that pollutes the air and can make people sick
It makes the rubbish disappear safely
questions.explanation: Burning rubbish releases toxic fumes and particles that pollute the air and can cause health problems.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think burning is a safe way to dispose of waste.

questions.stem: How does air pollution affect plants?
options: It can damage leaves and slow down growth
questions.explanation: Air pollutants can damage plant leaves and reduce their ability to make food, slowing growth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think pollution only affects humans.

questions.stem: What can a community do to reduce air pollution from vehicles?
options: Encourage walking, cycling, and using public transport
Cut down trees along the road
questions.explanation: Walking, cycling, and using public transport reduce the number of vehicles on the road, lowering air pollution.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think more cars are better.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a cause of air pollution?
questions.explanation: Planting trees is not a cause of air pollution; it helps reduce it.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all human activities pollute.

questions.stem: Name one human activity that pollutes the atmosphere.
hints: It comes from vehicles or factories.
questions.explanation: Burning rubbish, driving cars, and factory smoke are activities that pollute the atmosphere.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name a clean activity.

questions.stem: Name one way to reduce air pollution.
questions.explanation: Planting trees and reducing the burning of waste help reduce air pollution.

questions.stem: Why is air pollution a serious problem in big cities?
options: There are many cars and factories, leading to high levels of harmful gases
People in cities do not breathe
questions.explanation: High concentrations of vehicles and factories in cities release large amounts of pollutants into the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cities have cleaner air.

questions.stem: How does air pollution contribute to climate change?
options: Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere, causing the Earth to warm up
It has no effect on climate
hints: Gases like carbon dioxide trap heat.
questions.explanation: Pollutants like carbon dioxide are greenhouse gases that trap heat, contributing to global warming and climate change.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect air pollution to climate change.

questions.stem: Why is burning fossil fuels (like petrol) bad for the atmosphere?
options: It releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change
hints: Fossil fuels release gases when burned.
questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere and contributes to climate change.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know what fossil fuels are.

questions.stem: Write down two ways you can help reduce air pollution in your community.

criteria.description: States one action (e.g., planting trees, not burning rubbish)

questions.explanation: Planting trees and avoiding burning rubbish both help reduce air pollution.

questions.stem: Explain how smoke from vehicles and factories affects the atmosphere.

criteria.description: States that smoke releases harmful gases into the air
States that these gases pollute the air and can affect health and climate

hints: What comes out of exhaust pipes?
What does it do to the air?
questions.explanation: Smoke from vehicles and factories releases harmful gases that pollute the air and contribute to climate change.

questions.stem: A community is planning to reduce air pollution. Which strategy would be most effective?
options: Promoting the use of clean energy sources like solar power
Encouraging more people to burn their waste
Increasing the number of old vehicles on the road
hints: Solar power does not produce smoke.
It is a clean energy source.
questions.explanation: Using clean energy like solar power reduces the burning of fossil fuels, significantly lowering air pollution.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know about renewable energy.

questions.stem: Explain why cutting down trees can make air pollution worse.

criteria.description: States that trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen
States that fewer trees mean less carbon dioxide is removed from the air

hints: What do trees do with gases?
Why are trees important for clean air?
questions.explanation: Trees absorb carbon dioxide. Without them, more of this greenhouse gas remains in the atmosphere, worsening pollution and climate change.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher three human activities that pollute the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Burning rubbish, car exhaust, and factory smoke are common sources of air pollution.
